Senses.Explanation: A mass of doubt is something cultivated until it becomes concentrated and then breaks open or is shattered at awakening. The Chan record makes doubt materially mass-like: a discourse says that inside and outside ‘roll into one mass of doubt’ (滾作一箇疑團), and other records speak of making the whole body, sitting, walking, dressing, eating, and even the encountered world into that mass. The same physical grammar governs its end: it is ‘broken through’ (打破疑團), or remains ‘unbroken’ (疑團不破). In an autobiographical public account, repeated blows make Gaofeng Yuanmiao's mass of doubt more acute (疑團愈切). Thus the phrase is not merely ordinary uncertainty; these later Chan records deploy it as the consolidated, bodily condition named around sustained investigation and its reported breaking. The corpus does not make the mass a separate object from the doubt or state a further gloss for the breaking.

The phrase names a sustained, felt condition of doubt used in inquiry, not a passing uncertainty about a proposition. Wuyi Yuanlai explicitly asks what this doubt is and describes it erupting, knotting at the brows, and becoming impossible to put down or drive off. Dahui Zonggao says that while it remains unbroken, life and death press in. Gaofeng Yuanmiao recounts it suddenly arising while he held the question where the one returns, leaving him unable to distinguish directions. Librarian Lai tells Xueyan Zuqin that investigating Chan requires raising it and connects small doubt with small awakening. Preface author Ding Libiao calls not knowing a parent's destination or one's own beginning and end the great doubt of life and death shared across time. Zhongfeng Mingben warns that even uninterrupted conjunction of saying and doubt can become a subtle stealing mind. The corpus thus presents a concentrated condition to be raised and broken, while also warning against treating its continuity as achievement.
Senses.Note: Exact frozen-corpus count: 1,103 hits in 235 files and 230 works. Seven witnesses across six independent works meet the packet floor and cover definition, bodily description, unbroken condition, autobiography, instruction, preface formulation, and critique.

Senses.Explanation: The parent term's Chan use is verbal tangle; this orthographic form sharpens it to talk treated as idle or unnecessary. An early record warns people not to gather and talk idle vine-tangle, adding that the old man may catch and examine them. Two later verses call the whole great treasury of teachings 'idle vine-tangle': one immediately adds that the seventeen hundred cases trip people to death. A separate verse says that a massive volume already carries idle vine-tangle and puns that there is no need to send more 'idle furnishings.' The Zen deviation is the extension of the corpus's vine-language from individual words to gathered discussion, large books, the canon, and the case collection. The texts make those appraisals; this entry does not generalize them to every written record.

Senses.Explanation: The at-ease person of the Way appears chiefly in the compound “one at ease, with learning ended and nothing contrived,” which the records treat as a named condition rather than mere leisure. Literally, "an idle or at-ease person of the Way" . Chan usage bends ordinary idleness into a named epithet, most often in the full line "an at-ease person of the Way who has ended study and does nothing contrived" . Huangbo explains that people of old heard one statement and thereby "ended study" , and so received this name; he contrasts them with people seeking much knowledge and many explanations. Tianru explicitly lists "the great sea of extinction" , "the ground of actual principle" , and this full epithet as different names for "great rest" . The Mirror Record distinguishes accumulating study, ending study, and then passing beyond both, saying that only on reaching the end of study does one first draw near the Way. Other records deploy the shortened term in verse: the whole world is full of people seeking buddha, but an at-ease person of the Way is hard to find . The epithet therefore names a Chan roster type through explicit ending-study and great-rest definitions, not a generic loafer.
